components.note: 直 (straight, upright) — 真 relates to something level and true.
几 (a small table) — an object placed level and true on a table gave 真 its meaning 'real' or 'true.'
讠 (speech) — 话 relates to speaking and words.
舌 (tongue) — the organ used for speaking, reinforcing 话's meaning of 'speech' or 'words.'

example.hanzi: 面对失败,他终于说出了真话。
example.pinyin: miànduì shībài, tā zhōngyú shuōchūle zhēnhuà.
example.english: Facing failure, he finally told the truth.
example.fact: The polygraph, invented in the 1920s, does not actually detect lies — it measures heart rate, blood pressure, and skin conductivity, physiological markers of stress that can spike for many reasons besides deception. That is why U.S. federal courts have generally excluded polygraph results as evidence since the 1923 Frye ruling.

components.note: 子 (child) — 孤 originally described a child without a parent, an orphan.
瓜 (guā) gives a sound close to gū, sharing the same initial.
儿 (simplified from 兒) depicts a small child, drawn with a large head on a small body — a simple picture of youth.

example.hanzi: 这个慈善机构收养了很多孤儿。
example.pinyin: zhège císhàn jīgòu shōuyǎngle hěn duō gū'ér.
example.english: This charity has adopted many orphans.
example.fact: Kenya's Sheldrick Wildlife Trust runs one of the world's largest elephant orphanages, hand-raising calves whose mothers were killed by poachers or drought. Keepers sleep beside the young elephants at night, because in the wild a calf is almost never out of physical contact with an adult.

components.note: 心 (heart/mind) — 想 relates to thinking, missing someone, or wanting something in one's heart.
相 (xiāng) gives the sound — 想 is pronounced xiǎng, matching aside from tone.
亻 (person) — relates to 像's meaning 'to resemble, be like; image, portrait,' comparing one person or thing to another.
象 (xiàng) gives the sound — 像 is also pronounced xiàng, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 她想像自己站在舞台中央。
example.pinyin: tā xiǎngxiàng zìjǐ zhàn zài wǔtái zhōngyāng.
example.english: She imagined herself standing at the center of the stage.
example.fact: About 1 in 50 people have aphantasia, a condition in which the mind cannot generate visual images at all — asked to picture a red apple, they report just knowing the concept without any mental picture. The trait was only formally named by neurologist Adam Zeman in 2015, even though it had presumably always existed.

components.note: A short stroke placed below a longer one — the mirror image of 上 (up), together forming a simple, opposite pair.

巴's oracle-bone form is usually read as a picture of a large serpent, tied to old legends of a giant snake swallowing an elephant whole. The character was later borrowed mainly for its sound, in words like 下巴 and 尾巴, with little trace of the original picture left.

example.hanzi: 他摸着下巴思考了很久。
example.pinyin: tā mōzhe xiàba sīkǎole hěn jiǔ.
example.english: He stroked his chin and thought for a long time.
example.fact: The bony chin is a feature unique to Homo sapiens among all primates — even Neanderthals lacked a true chin. Anthropologists still debate why it evolved, with theories ranging from chewing mechanics to a byproduct of the face shrinking as our jaws grew smaller relative to the rest of the skull.

components.note: 发 is the simplified form of 發, which combined 弓 (a bow, hinting at the idea of letting an arrow fly) with 癹 as a sound-bearing element. Simplification collapsed both parts into a few strokes, so the modern shape no longer shows the original picture of shooting or releasing something.
氵 (water) — leaking is described using the water radical, whether literal or figurative.
世 (shì) gives a sound distantly related to xiè, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 他靠打拳发泄心中的怒气。
example.pinyin: tā kào dǎquán fāxiè xīnzhōng de nùqì.
example.english: He vents his anger by boxing.
example.fact: For decades, pop psychology claimed that punching a pillow or screaming helps 'let out' anger, but controlled studies by psychologist Brad Bushman in the early 2000s found the opposite: people who vented aggressively afterward became more angry, not less, because the act of venting rehearses and reinforces the aggressive response rather than releasing it.

components.note: 心 (heart) — 恐 describes fear felt in the heart.
巩 (gǒng) gives a sound close to kǒng, sharing the same rhyme.
口 (mouth) — 吓 relates to a shout or cry, as when someone is frightened.
下 (xià) gives the sound — an exact match with 吓.

example.hanzi: 他收到了一封恐吓信。
example.pinyin: tā shōudàole yī fēng kǒnghè xìn.
example.english: He received a threatening letter.
example.fact: Rattlesnakes evolved their tail rattle mainly as a bluff — studies show the sound is meant to avoid a costly fight, not to announce an imminent strike. Snakes that are cornered and truly threatened often strike silently instead, saving the rattle for situations where a warning might still let both animals walk away.

components.note: 彡 (fine lines) — suggests light and shadow, relating to 影's meaning 'shadow, image.'
景 (jǐng) gives a sound hint — 影 is pronounced yǐng, sharing the same rhyme though the initial consonant differs.
亻 (person) — relates to 像's meaning 'to resemble, be like; image, portrait,' comparing one person or thing to another.
象 (xiàng) gives the sound — 像 is also pronounced xiàng, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 医生正在分析X光影像。
example.pinyin: yīshēng zhèngzài fēnxī X guāng yǐngxiàng.
example.english: The doctor is analyzing the X-ray images.
example.fact: In December 1895, physicist Wilhelm Röntgen produced the first X-ray image ever made — a photograph of his wife Anna Bertha's hand, showing her bones and wedding ring in ghostly outline. The discovery earned him the very first Nobel Prize in Physics in 1901.

components.note: 氵 (water) — relates to 清's meaning 'clear (water), pure.'
青 (qīng) gives the sound — 清 is also pronounced qīng, an exact match.
氵 (water) — 洁 describes something washed and made clean and pure.
吉 (jí) gives a sound close to jié, sharing the initial — the rhyme has drifted slightly from í to ié.

example.hanzi: 每天早上她都会清洁厨房。
example.pinyin: měitiān zǎoshang tā dūhuì qīngjié chúfáng.
example.english: Every morning she cleans the kitchen.
example.fact: In 1847, Hungarian physician Ignaz Semmelweis discovered that doctors who washed their hands with a chlorinated lime solution before delivering babies cut maternal deaths from childbed fever nearly tenfold. His colleagues mocked the idea, and he died in an asylum years before germ theory finally proved him right.

components.note: 口 is a simple picture of an open mouth.
彳 (to walk, step) — 径 names a small path for walking.
工 (gōng) gives a sound distantly related to jìng, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 这架望远镜的口径达到了八米。
example.pinyin: zhè jià wàngyuǎnjìng de kǒujìng dádàole bā mǐ.
example.english: This telescope's aperture reaches eight meters.
example.fact: A telescope's resolving power depends almost entirely on its aperture, or 口径 — doubling the diameter of the primary mirror quadruples the light-gathering area. The Extremely Large Telescope under construction in Chile, with a 39-meter mirror built from 798 hexagonal segments, will see roughly 100 million times fainter objects than the naked eye.

components.note: 立 (standing) — a small figure standing upright.
里 here representing a village or settlement, together giving 童 its meaning 'child.'
干 (originally a person) shown carrying a heavy load of grain on their back — since harvests came once a year, the character came to mean 'year.'

example.hanzi: 他常常怀念自己的童年。
example.pinyin: tā chángcháng huáiniàn zìjǐ de tóngnián.
example.english: He often reminisces about his childhood.
example.fact: Historian Philippe Ariès argued in his 1960 book Centuries of Childhood that medieval European societies had little concept of childhood as a distinct stage of life — children were largely treated as small, incompetent adults, and the idea of a protected, separate childhood only solidified in the 17th and 18th centuries.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 哈 is the sound made by the mouth while laughing
合 (hé) gives a sound related to 哈's reading hā, from an older, closer pronunciation link
亻 (person) — 佛 refers to an enlightened being, the Buddha
弗 (fú) gives the sound — an exact match with 佛's reading fú

example.hanzi: 他被哈佛大学录取了。
example.pinyin: tā bèi Hāfó dàxué lùqǔle.
example.english: He was admitted to Harvard University.
example.fact: Founded in 1636, Harvard University is the oldest institution of higher education in the United States, established more than a century before the country itself. It takes its name from John Harvard, a young clergyman whose donation of his library and half his estate after his 1638 death was, at the time, one of the largest gifts the fledgling college had received.

components.note: 口 (mouths) — 总 pictures many voices.
心 (heart, mind) — many mouths brought together under one mind gave 总 its meaning 'overall' or 'to gather together.'
戈 (a blade) — 裁 involves cutting.
衣 (clothing) — cutting cloth to make or trim clothing, giving 裁 its meaning 'to cut out, to reduce.'

example.hanzi: 这位总裁决定裁员一千人。
example.pinyin: zhè wèi zǒngcái juédìng cáiyuán yī qiān rén.
example.english: This chairman decided to lay off a thousand employees.
example.fact: Kongō Gumi, a Japanese construction firm founded in 578 CE to build Buddhist temples, was run by the same family for over 1,400 years, making it one of the longest continuously operating companies in history before it became a subsidiary of a larger construction group in 2006.

components.note: 羊 (sheep) — 羞 pairs a sheep with the idea of something unsightly.
丑 (ugly, shameful) contributes to the character's form, giving 羞 its meaning 'ashamed, shy.'
耳 (ear) — an old sense linked shame to the reddening of the ears.
止 (zhǐ) gives a sound close to chǐ, sharing the same rhyme though the initial has shifted.

example.hanzi: 撒谎后他感到十分羞耻。
example.pinyin: sāhuǎng hòu tā gǎndào shífēn xiūchǐ.
example.english: After lying, he felt deeply ashamed.
example.fact: Charles Darwin devoted an entire chapter of his 1872 book The Expression of the Emotions to blushing, calling it 'the most peculiar and the most human of all expressions.' Blushing is involuntary and visible mainly on the face, and unlike most emotional displays, no other animal is known to do it.

components.note: 辶 (to walk) — 追 relates to moving in pursuit of someone or something
㠯 (yǐ) gives a sound distantly related to 追's reading zhuī, having drifted apart over time
扌 (hand) — 捕 describes catching something with the hands.
甫 (fǔ) gives a sound close to bǔ, sharing the same kind of initial consonant.

example.hanzi: 警方正在追捕逃犯。
example.pinyin: jǐngfāng zhèngzài zhuībǔ táofàn.
example.english: The police are hunting down the escaped criminal.
example.fact: Bloodhounds have roughly 300 million scent receptors, compared to about 6 million in humans, and their tracking ability is considered so reliable that many U.S. courts allow bloodhound-trail evidence in criminal trials — some documented trails have been successfully followed hundreds of hours after a person walked through.

components.note: 尸 (a body) — the body of an animal.
毛 (fur/hair) — trailing behind it, together giving 尾 its meaning 'tail.'

巴's oracle-bone form is usually read as a picture of a large serpent, tied to old legends of a giant snake swallowing an elephant whole. The character was later borrowed mainly for its sound, in words like 下巴 and 尾巴, with little trace of the original picture left.

example.hanzi: 小狗高兴地摇着尾巴。
example.pinyin: xiǎo gǒu gāoxìng de yáozhe wěiba.
example.english: The puppy happily wagged its tail.
example.fact: A 2014 study using force-plate treadmills found that kangaroos push off the ground with their tails with as much force as an average human leg produces while walking — effectively making the tail a fifth limb rather than just a tool for balance.

components.note: 见 (to see) — relates directly to 视's meaning 'to look at, view.'
礻 (a form of 示, shì) gives the sound — 视 is also pronounced shì, an exact match.
纟 (thread) — relates directly to 线's meaning 'line, thread, wire.'
戋 (jiān) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from xiàn.

example.hanzi: 一棵大树挡住了我们的视线。
example.pinyin: yī kē dà shù dǎngzhùle wǒmen de shìxiàn.
example.english: A big tree blocked our line of sight.
example.fact: Because light travels in straight lines while Earth's surface curves away beneath it, a ship's lookout standing ten meters above the waterline can only see a lighthouse's beam after cresting the horizon. That is why classic lighthouses were built as tall as possible — extra height extends the line of sight for miles farther out to sea.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) shows 帐 relates to something made of fabric, like a tent or curtain.
长 (zhǎng) gives a sound close to zhàng, sharing the initial consonant.
⺮ (bamboo) — 篷 was traditionally made of woven bamboo.
逢 (féng) gives a sound close to péng, sharing a related initial sound.

example.hanzi: 我们在山顶搭起了帐篷。
example.pinyin: wǒmen zài shāndǐng dāqǐle zhàngpeng.
example.english: We set up a tent on the mountaintop.
example.fact: Mongolian gers (yurts) are engineered so a family can dismantle the entire structure — lattice walls, roof poles, and felt covering — and pack it onto a single camel or cart in under two hours, a design perfected over centuries of seasonal migration across the steppe.

meanings: (fig.) a person's established path in life

components.note: Cart/vehicle — tracks are made by wheels.
Gives the sound jiǔ, related to guǐ but drifted apart over time.
辶 (to walk) — 道 relates to a path or road one walks along.
首 (shǒu) is the historical phonetic element; its modern reading no longer resembles dào, a reminder that sound components can drift after thousands of years of pronunciation change.

example.hanzi: 这颗卫星正沿着固定轨道运行。
example.pinyin: zhè kē wèixīng zhèng yánzhe gùdìng guǐdào yùnxíng.
example.english: This satellite is moving along a fixed orbit.
example.fact: A satellite placed in geostationary orbit, about 35,786 kilometers above the equator, takes exactly 23 hours 56 minutes to complete one loop — matching Earth's rotation so precisely that it appears to hang motionless over the same spot on the ground, which is why satellite dishes never need to move.

components.note: 刀 (knife) — 剪 names a cutting tool, scissors.
前 (qián) is close in initial to jiǎn (q-/j- are a related palatal family), though the rhyme has drifted.
刀 is a simple line drawing of a single-edged blade with a curved handle, one of the most basic pictographs in the script.

example.hanzi: 她用剪刀剪断了绳子。
example.pinyin: tā yòng jiǎndāo jiǎnduànle shéngzi.
example.english: She cut the rope with scissors.
example.fact: The earliest scissors, found in Mesopotamia roughly 3,000 years ago, were spring-action tools made from a single strip of bronze bent into two blades that snapped shut. The pivoted, cross-bladed design familiar today, with a fixed pin joining two separate blades, was a later Roman innovation that appeared around 100 CE.

components.note: 灬 (fire) — 点 originally related to a small flame or dot of light, giving rise to the meaning 'dot' or 'point.'
占 (zhàn) gives a hint of the sound — 点 is pronounced diǎn, a connection that has drifted over the centuries.
心 was originally a pictograph of the physical shape of a human heart, and came to represent the mind, feelings, and intention as well.

example.hanzi: 周末我们全家去饭馆吃点心。
example.pinyin: zhōumò wǒmen quánjiā qù fànguǎn chī diǎnxin.
example.english: On the weekend our whole family goes to a restaurant to eat dim sum.
example.fact: Dim sum's tradition of small dishes eaten alongside tea, known as 'yum cha,' is believed to have grown out of roadside teahouses along the ancient Silk Road, where travelers stopped to rest their horses and were served tea with light snacks — a custom Cantonese culture later refined into today's elaborate multi-course tea brunch.

components.note: 上 (top) — the upper edge pressing down
卜 — the lower edge, with a card squeezed between the two
亻 (person) — the one settling somewhere.
主 (host, master) — the idea of a person settled in a place as if hosting it, giving 住 its meaning 'to live, reside, stay.'

example.hanzi: 钥匙卡住了,打不开门。
example.pinyin: yàoshi kǎzhùle, dǎ bù kāi mén.
example.english: The key got stuck, and the door won't open.
example.fact: In March 2021, the container ship Ever Given ran aground and wedged sideways across the Suez Canal, blocking one of the world's busiest shipping lanes for six days. The jam held up an estimated $9.6 billion in trade every single day it remained stuck, rippling through global supply chains for months afterward.

components.note: Gas — oxygen is a type of gas.
Gives the sound yáng, related to yǎng but drifted apart over time.
气 (simplified from 氣) depicts rising wisps or vapor, like breath or steam drifting upward — a simple picture of air or gas.

example.hanzi: 医生给病人吸上了氧气。
example.pinyin: yīshēng gěi bìngrén xīshàngle yǎngqì.
example.english: The doctor put the patient on oxygen.
example.fact: Earth's atmosphere was not always oxygen-rich — for roughly the first two billion years of the planet's history it contained almost none. Photosynthesizing cyanobacteria slowly changed that during the Great Oxidation Event around 2.4 billion years ago, a shift so severe it wiped out most of the anaerobic life that had dominated until then.

components.note: 辶 (to walk, to move) — suggests departing or leaving.
贵 (valuable, precious) — leaving something valuable behind gave 遗 its meaning 'to lose, to leave behind.'
亻 (person) — relates to 传's meaning 'to pass on, transmit,' something passed from person to person.
专 (zhuān) gives a sound hint — 传 is pronounced chuán, sharing the same rhyme though the initial consonant differs.

example.hanzi: 这种疾病可能通过基因遗传给后代。
example.pinyin: zhè zhǒng jíbìng kěnéng tōngguò jīyīn yíchuán gěi hòudài.
example.english: This disease can be genetically inherited by future generations.
example.fact: Gregor Mendel, an Austrian monk, spent eight years in the 1850s and 1860s cross-breeding thousands of pea plants in his monastery garden, tracking traits like flower color and seed shape across generations. His statistical patterns, largely ignored during his lifetime, were rediscovered around 1900 and became the foundation of modern genetics.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 抽 describes pulling something out with the hand.
由 (yóu) gives a sound distantly related to chōu, having drifted apart over time.
尸 here stands in for a flat, body-like covering rather than its literal sense of 'corpse' — hinting at the shallow, flat shape of a drawer or tray.
由 (yóu) is only distantly related in sound to 屉's reading tì, the two syllables having drifted apart over the centuries, so the phonetic link is mostly historical now.

example.hanzi: 他把文件放进了抽屉里。
example.pinyin: tā bǎ wénjiàn fàng jìnle chōuti lǐ.
example.english: He put the documents into the drawer.
example.fact: The modern drawer with smooth ball-bearing slides is a surprisingly recent invention — it did not become common in furniture until the mid-20th century. Before that, drawers ran on plain wood-to-wood friction, which is why old dressers so often stick or need to be pulled at an angle to open.

components.note: 囗 depicts an enclosure or fence.
木 (tree) — a tree hemmed in by a fence, unable to grow freely, gave 困 its meaning 'trapped, difficult.'
土 (earth) — 境 relates to land and territory, extended to mean 'environment, boundary'
竟 (jìng) gives the sound — 境 is also pronounced jìng, an exact match

example.hanzi: 公司目前陷入了财务困境。
example.pinyin: gōngsī mùqián xiànrùle cáiwù kùnjìng.
example.english: The company is currently caught in a financial predicament.
example.fact: The prisoner's dilemma, one of the most famous predicaments in game theory, was formalized in 1950 by mathematicians Merrill Flood and Melvin Dresher at the RAND Corporation while researching nuclear strategy. It shows how two rational people acting purely in self-interest can end up worse off than if they had cooperated.

components.note: 大 (big) — in 头's simplified form, this element is linked to the idea of 'high' or topmost, since the head sits at the top of the body.
纟 (thread) — 绪 originally meant the end of a thread, extending to 'clue, beginnings.'
者 (zhě) gives a sound distantly related to xù's reading, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 这个案子毫无头绪。
example.pinyin: zhège ànzi háowú tóuxù.
example.english: This case has no leads at all.
example.fact: Forensic science largely rests on Locard's exchange principle, formulated by French criminologist Edmond Locard around 1910: every person who enters a crime scene both brings something into it and takes something away, however microscopic — a principle that underlies modern fiber, fingerprint, and DNA analysis.

components.note: 皿 (a vessel) — a chalice or bowl
丿 — a single drop of blood inside the vessel
土 (soil) — earth being pressed down
厂 (a cliff/overhang) — a heavy mass bearing down from above

example.hanzi: 医生每天都要给病人测血压。
example.pinyin: yīshēng měitiān dōu yào gěi bìngrén cè xuèyā.
example.english: The doctor measures the patient's blood pressure every day.
example.fact: Giraffes have the highest blood pressure of any mammal, roughly two to three times that of humans, because their hearts must pump blood nearly two meters up their long necks to reach the brain. Thick, elastic vessel walls and a tight sheath of skin around their lower legs keep this pressure from causing swelling when they lower their heads to drink.

components.note: 十's earliest form was a single vertical stroke, likely representing a knot tied into a cord — ancient tally-keepers marked off groups of ten items by tying a knot, and the knot mark itself became the number 十.
足 depicts a leg (the upper shape) above a foot — a simple picture of the human leg and foot, giving 足 its meaning 'foot, to be sufficient.'

example.hanzi: 他对这次比赛信心十足。
example.pinyin: tā duì zhè cì bǐsài xìnxīn shízú.
example.english: He is fully confident about this competition.
example.fact: Roughly 90% of the world's languages use a base-10 (decimal) counting system, almost certainly because humans have ten fingers to count on. A notable exception is the ancient Maya, who developed a base-20 system, likely by counting fingers and toes together.

components.note: 人 (people) over 云 (clouds/say) — a picture of people gathering and speaking together, related to 会's meanings 'to meet' and 'to know how to.'
贝 (shell/money — cowrie shells were historically used as currency) — 员 originally related to counting or officials responsible for accounts, later broadening to mean 'member' or 'personnel.'

example.hanzi: 她刚办了健身房的会员卡。
example.pinyin: tā gāng bànle jiànshēnfáng de huìyuán kǎ.
example.english: She just got a membership card for the gym.
example.fact: The Royal Society, founded in London in 1660, is the oldest continuously existing national scientific institution in the world. Its early fellows included Isaac Newton and Robert Boyle, and to this day new members are still inducted by signing the same charter book used since the society's founding.

components.note: 长 (simplified from 長) depicts an elderly figure with long flowing hair and a cane — length and seniority are linked in the original picture.
月 (moon) — 期 relates to time measured by the moon's cycles, like a period or term.
其 (qí) gives a hint of the sound — 期 is pronounced qī, a connection that has shifted slightly in tone.

example.hanzi: 长期熬夜对身体不好。
example.pinyin: chángqī áoyè duì shēntǐ bù hǎo.
example.english: Staying up late for a long time is bad for your health.
example.fact: The Broadbalk Wheat Experiment at Rothamsted Research in England has been running continuously since 1843, making it the longest-running agricultural field experiment in the world. Researchers have tracked the same plots' soil and crop yields under different fertilizer treatments for more than 180 years.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — relates directly to 拉's meaning 'to pull, drag,' an action done by hand.
立 (lì) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted noticeably from lā.
扌 (hand) — relates directly to 拉's meaning 'to pull, drag,' an action done by hand.
立 (lì) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted noticeably from lā.

example.hanzi: 他家养了一只可爱的拉拉。
example.pinyin: tā jiā yǎngle yī zhī kě'ài de lālā.
example.english: His family keeps an adorable Labrador retriever.
example.fact: Despite the name, Labrador retrievers did not originate in Labrador but in Newfoundland, Canada, where fishermen bred them in the 1700s to retrieve fish and haul nets from the icy North Atlantic waters. British aristocrats imported the breed in the 19th century and refined it into the dog known today.

components.note: A vertical line 丨 running through the middle of a box or flag 口 — a simple image for the idea of 'center, middle.'
冖 (a covering/roof) — represents the building or schoolhouse where learning happens.
子 (child) — 学 depicts children gathered to study.
⺍ is a small graphic element at the top of the character; its original pictorial meaning, if any, has been lost over time.

example.hanzi: 他明年就要上中学了。
example.pinyin: tā míngnián jiù yào shàng zhōngxué le.
example.english: He will start middle school next year.
example.fact: Eton College in England, founded by King Henry VI in 1440, has operated continuously as a secondary school for over 580 years, making it one of the oldest schools in the world still teaching students today.

components.note: 勾 began as a simple picture of a bent or hooked line, the shape of a hook itself, which is why it still means 'hook' and 'to hook, entice' today.
弓 (bow) — the weapon being drawn.
丨 depicts the taut drawstring being pulled back — giving 引 its meaning 'to pull, draw out, attract.'

example.hanzi: 广告常常用美食图片勾引消费者购买。
example.pinyin: guǎnggào chángcháng yòng měishí túpiàn gōuyǐn xiāofèizhě gòumǎi.
example.english: Advertisements often use pictures of delicious food to tempt consumers into buying.
example.fact: Deep-sea anglerfish dangle a bioluminescent lure, called an esca, above their mouths to attract curious prey in the pitch-black ocean depths. The light comes from colonies of symbiotic bacteria living inside the lure, which the anglerfish cannot produce on its own.

components.note: 匕 here relates to a person crouching or sitting — 此 originally pictured 'this place' where someone is.
止 (zhǐ) gives a hint of the sound — 此 is pronounced cǐ, sharing a similar final though the initial has shifted over time.
事's early form pictured a hand grasping a forked pole or tally used by scribes to record official business, so the character first meant an official duty before broadening to 'matter, affair.'

example.hanzi: 领导表示会认真调查此事。
example.pinyin: lǐngdǎo biǎoshì huì rènzhēn diàochá cǐshì.
example.english: The leader said they would seriously investigate this matter.
example.fact: The official investigations into the 1912 sinking of the Titanic led directly to the first International Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea (SOLAS) in 1914, which mandated lifeboat space for every passenger and round-the-clock radio watches. Updated versions of that same treaty still govern maritime safety worldwide today.

components.note: 巨 depicts a hand gripping a large carpenter's square, a tool for measuring right angles — an image linked to great size, giving 巨 its meaning 'huge, giant.'
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.

example.hanzi: 传说中山里住着一个巨人。
example.pinyin: chuánshuō zhōng shānlǐ zhùzhe yī gè jùrén.
example.english: According to legend, a giant lives in the mountains.
example.fact: Robert Wadlow, born in Illinois in 1918, is the tallest person ever reliably recorded at 8 feet 11 inches (2.72 meters). His extraordinary growth was caused by a pituitary tumor that continuously released growth hormone; he was still growing when he died at age 22.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — carrying something along is done by hand.
隽 (juàn in related readings) gives a sound distantly related to xié, having drifted apart over time.
巾 (cloth) — the bottom half of a belt, hanging straight down.
Above the cloth, the strokes crease as if folded at the waist — depicting a belt or sash, the source of 带's meaning 'belt, band,' later 'to bring, carry along.'

example.hanzi: 出国旅行时请随身携带护照。
example.pinyin: chūguó lǚxíng shí qǐng suíshēn xiédài hùzhào.
example.english: When traveling abroad, please carry your passport with you.
example.fact: A camel's hump doesn't store water, as commonly believed — it stores fat, which the animal can convert into energy and metabolic water during long desert crossings. This adaptation lets a camel carry a heavy load and go without drinking for over a week in extreme heat.

components.note: 心 (heart/mind) — 急 relates to an anxious or urgent state of mind
刍 (chú) gives a sound distantly related to 急's reading jí, having drifted apart over time
攵 (a hand taking action) — 救 describes the act of rescuing someone.
求 (qiú) gives a sound close to jiù, sharing a similar rhyme.

example.hanzi: 学校组织了一次急救培训课程。
example.pinyin: xuéxiào zǔzhīle yī cì jíjiù péixùn kèchéng.
example.english: The school organized a first-aid training course.
example.fact: Modern CPR as taught today was developed in the late 1950s and early 1960s by physicians Peter Safar and James Elam, who combined mouth-to-mouth ventilation with chest compressions into a single technique. Safar's 1957 book laid the basis for CPR training used worldwide.

components.note: 马 (simplified from 馬) depicts a horse in profile, with its mane, legs, and tail visible — later simplified into just a few strokes.
A simplified form of 車, a pictograph of a two-wheeled cart seen from above — the wheels, axle, and frame are visible in the original shape — the source of 车's meaning 'cart, vehicle.'

example.hanzi: 古代的贵族喜欢乘坐马车出行。
example.pinyin: gǔdài de guìzú xǐhuān chéngzuò mǎchē chūxíng.
example.english: Ancient aristocrats liked to travel by carriage.
example.fact: The earliest wheeled vehicles, dating to around 3500 BCE in Mesopotamia, used solid wooden wheels that were heavy and slow. The lighter spoked wheel wasn't invented until roughly 2000 BCE, and it revolutionized warfare by making fast, maneuverable horse-drawn chariots possible.

components.note: 宀 (walls/roof) — the boundary of a home to be protected
寸 (a hand) — keeping watch, holding the space within the walls
扌 (hand) — represents the act of guarding or defending.
户 (door/household) — protecting one's home gave 护 its meaning 'to protect, guard.'

example.hanzi: 士兵们日夜守护着边境。
example.pinyin: shìbīngmen rìyè shǒuhùzhe biānjìng.
example.english: The soldiers guard the border day and night.
example.fact: A 2012 Chinese government survey measured the total length of all sections, branches, and spurs of the Great Wall of China, built and rebuilt over more than two thousand years to guard the northern frontier, at over 21,000 kilometers — more than half the Earth's circumference.

components.note: The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'
日 (sun) — combined with 月 (moon), 明 shows the light of both sun and moon, giving the meaning 'bright' or 'clear.'
月 (moon) — together with 日 (sun), the two brightest things in the sky represent brightness and clarity.

example.hanzi: 事故的原因目前仍然不明。
example.pinyin: shìgù de yuányīn mùqián réngrán bùmíng.
example.english: The cause of the accident is still unclear at present.
example.fact: Ball lightning — glowing, floating spheres of light reported during thunderstorms for centuries — remains scientifically unexplained. Despite hundreds of eyewitness accounts and several competing hypotheses involving plasma or vaporized silicon, no laboratory experiment has yet reliably reproduced anything matching the reported behavior.

components.note: 隹 (a bird) sits above, the thing being affected by fire.
灬 (flames) beneath shows fire scorching it, giving 焦 its meaning 'burnt, scorched' and later 'anxious.'
虍 depicts a tiger's head or stripes.
心 (heart) — a heart facing a tiger's threat gave 虑 its meaning 'to worry, to be concerned.'

example.hanzi: 考试前她感到非常焦虑。
example.pinyin: kǎoshì qián tā gǎndào fēicháng jiāolǜ.
example.english: Before the exam she felt very anxious.
example.fact: Hungarian-Canadian endocrinologist Hans Selye coined the term 'stress' in its modern psychological sense in 1936, describing what he called the 'general adaptation syndrome' — the body's three-stage hormonal response to prolonged threat. His work laid the foundation for later research into cortisol and chronic anxiety.

components.note: 犭 (dog/animal) — 狡 groups cunning behavior with animal-related characters.
交 (jiāo) gives a sound close to jiǎo, the same syllable with a different tone.
犭 (dog, beast) — 猾 (crafty, cunning) was traditionally likened to a wild animal's slyness.
骨 (gǔ) gives a sound only distantly related to huá today, a connection that has faded over roughly three millennia of sound change.

example.hanzi: 狐狸是出了名的狡猾动物。
example.pinyin: húli shì chūle míng de jiǎohuá dòngwù.
example.english: The fox is a famously cunning animal.
example.fact: New Caledonian crows are among the few non-human animals known to manufacture tools rather than just use them, bending twigs into hooks to pull insect larvae from crevices. Ravens go further still, sometimes pretending to hide food in a false spot while a rival watches, only to sneak the real food away once the rival gives up on the decoy.

meanings: see 海倫市|海伦市[Hai3 lun2 Shi4]

components.note: 氵 (water) — 海 relates to bodies of water, specifically the sea.
每 (měi) gives a hint of the sound — 海 is pronounced hǎi, a connection that has shifted over time.
亻 (person) — 伦 relates to human relationships and social order.
仑 depicts an orderly, logical arrangement — combined with 亻, giving 伦 its meaning 'human relationships, order.'

example.hanzi: 海伦是我们班新来的交换生。
example.pinyin: Hǎilún shì wǒmen bān xīnlái de jiāohuànshēng.
example.english: Helen is the new exchange student in our class.
example.fact: Helen Keller, who became deaf and blind after an illness at 19 months old, learned to read, write, and speak with the help of her teacher Anne Sullivan. In 1904 she became the first deafblind person to earn a bachelor's degree, graduating cum laude from Radcliffe College.

meanings: to embezzle by making illegal deductions

components.note: 刂 (a knife) — 刻 relates to carving with a blade
亥 (hài) is the historical phonetic element; it no longer closely matches 刻's modern reading kè
艹 (plant) — 薄 originally described sparse, thin grass, extending to 'thin' in general.
溥 (pǔ) is only distantly related in sound to báo — the rhyme has drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 他说话总是很刻薄。
example.pinyin: tā shuōhuà zǒngshì hěn kèbó.
example.english: He always speaks harshly.
example.fact: Psychologist John Suler coined the term 'online disinhibition effect' in 2004 to describe why people are often far harsher and blunter in text-based communication than they would ever be face to face — the anonymity, invisibility, and lack of immediate consequence online loosen normal social restraint.

components.note: 木 (wood) — 检 originally related to a wooden tally or label used for checking records
佥 (qiān) gives a sound distantly related to 检's reading jiǎn, having drifted apart over time
马 (horse) — 验 originally related to examining or testing horses, later extended to 'to test, examine, verify'
佥 (qiān) gives a loose sound connection to 验's reading yàn

example.hanzi: 每批产品出厂前都要经过严格检验。
example.pinyin: měi pī chǎnpǐn chūchǎng qián dōu yào jīngguò yángé jiǎnyàn.
example.english: Every batch of products must undergo strict inspection before leaving the factory.
example.fact: The quality-control philosophy known as Six Sigma was developed at Motorola in 1986 by engineer Bill Smith, aiming to reduce manufacturing defects to fewer than 3.4 per million opportunities. The method later spread across global industry after General Electric adopted it company-wide in the mid-1990s under CEO Jack Welch.

components.note: 辶 (to walk/move) — shows 过's core meaning of 'passing through' or 'crossing'
咼 (guō) gives a sound close to 过's reading guò; the simplified form 过 now uses 寸 in place of 咼, but the phonetic connection traces back to the traditional character 過
世 depicts three leaves or shoots on a stem, suggesting continuous growth across generations — giving rise to the meaning 'generation' or 'world.'

example.hanzi: 他的祖父上个月过世了。
example.pinyin: tā de zǔfù shàng gè yuè guòshìle.
example.english: His grandfather passed away last month.
example.fact: Global average life expectancy at birth was only about 32 years in 1900; by 2019 it had more than doubled to over 72 years, one of the most dramatic improvements in human welfare ever recorded, driven mainly by reductions in infant and child mortality rather than people simply living much longer once they reached adulthood.

meanings: Texas (abbr. for 德克薩斯州|德克萨斯州[De2 ke4 sa4 si1 Zhou1])

components.note: 心 (heart/mind) — 德 relates to inner moral character and virtue.
州 depicts small dots of land, like islands, surrounded by the curving lines of a river (川) — the origin of its meaning 'state, region.'

example.hanzi: 他去年搬到了德州休斯顿。
example.pinyin: tā qùnián bāndàole Dézhōu Xiūsīdùn.
example.english: He moved to Houston, Texas, last year.
example.fact: Texas is the only U.S. state that was once an independent, internationally recognized nation — the Republic of Texas existed from 1836 to 1845 after winning independence from Mexico, before voluntarily joining the United States as its 28th state.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 误 began as a mistake in speech, later broadening to 'error' in general.
吴 (wú) gives a sound close to wù, with the tone shifted.
角 (horn) — 解 pictures removing a part of an animal.
牛 (ox) — together with a knife cutting between horn and ox, 解 pictures separating something into parts, giving its meaning 'to untie' or 'to explain.'

example.hanzi: 她因为误解朋友的话而生气了。
example.pinyin: tā yīnwèi wùjiě péngyou de huà ér shēngqìle.
example.english: She got angry because she misunderstood her friend's words.
example.fact: Neil Armstrong always insisted he said 'That's one small step for a man, one giant leap for mankind' during the 1969 moon landing, but the crucial word 'a' is inaudible on the recording, leading to decades of debate among audio engineers and linguists about whether it was ever spoken or simply lost to static.

components.note: 金 (metal) reflects 鉴's original meaning "a bronze mirror," an object made of metal.

于 (simplified from 於) is thought to have originally pictured a bent wind instrument or tool; the character was later borrowed purely for its sound to serve as the grammatical preposition 'at, in, than,' with the original picture fading from use.

example.hanzi: 鉴于天气恶劣,比赛被迫取消。
example.pinyin: jiànyú tiānqì èliè, bǐsài bèipò qǔxiāo.
example.english: In view of the bad weather, the match was forced to be canceled.
example.fact: Five-day weather forecasts today are as accurate as one-day forecasts were in the 1980s, thanks to satellite data, greater computing power, and improved atmospheric models — a jump that has saved countless lives and dollars by giving communities more advance warning before major storms.

components.note: 凡 (fán) is close in sound to the traditional character 風's reading fēng, sharing the same initial, and the same outline was carried over into the simplified 风.

The traditional form 風 enclosed 虫 (an insect) inside, reflecting an ancient belief that wind bred insects; simplification dropped the insect and kept only the outer shape, so 风's modern form no longer shows this semantic link directly.
日 (the sun) — sunlight falling over the land
京 (a capital city) — a grand city view worth seeing

example.hanzi: 站在山顶,风景美得令人窒息。
example.pinyin: zhàn zài shāndǐng, fēngjǐng měi de lìng rén zhìxī.
example.english: Standing on the mountaintop, the scenery is breathtakingly beautiful.
example.fact: The dramatic karst pinnacles of Zhangjiajie National Forest Park in China, shaped over roughly 300 million years by the erosion of quartz-sandstone, directly inspired the floating 'Hallelujah Mountains' in James Cameron's 2009 film Avatar — the park even renamed one of its peaks 'Avatar Hallelujah Mountain' afterward.
